title: Telecommunications Legislation Amendment (Consumer Protection) Bill 2013
portfolio: Broadband, Communications and the Digital Economy

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would change telecommunications consumer protection rules by revising oversight of the Telecommunications Industry Ombudsman, industry code procedures and responsibility for outsourced marketing.
It would let the Minister set ombudsman standards, require independent public reviews and allow registered industry codes to be varied instead of replaced.
Code and marketing changes would start after Royal Assent, while ombudsman provisions would commence by proclamation or after a six-month fallback period.
changes: The first ombudsman review would be due within three years, followed by reviews every five years.
Code developers would have to publish draft codes, draft variations and consultation submissions on their websites, except for minor draft variations.
Reimbursement of eligible code development costs would extend to code variations.
Marketing arrangements could attract Do Not Call Register obligations without expressly mentioning telemarketing calls or marketing faxes.
summary.affected: Telecommunications consumers, carriers, service providers, code developers and businesses commissioning telemarketing or fax marketing are affected.

speeches.speaker: Anthony Albanese
speeches.brief: Moved the bill to strengthen telecommunications consumer protections by improving enforcement of the Do Not Call Register Act 2006, allowing industry codes to be varied, increasing transparency in code development, and requiring standards and independent reviews for the Telecommunications Industry Ombudsman scheme.
